## Purpose
The SQLite tables around the Neo4j graph: tracked documents and their processing state, extraction drafts, versioned per-library ontologies, per-library extraction rules, platform-owned system agents, and the processing timeline.

## Responsibilities
- **`DOCUMENT_STATUSES`**, in lifecycle order:
  - uploaded, indexing, extracted, extracting, proposed, graphed;
  - unsupported (the library returned no text; there is no OCR fallback, by design);
  - failed.
- **`UNGRAPHED_STATUSES`** is every status except graphed.
- **`RagDocument` (`rag_documents`):**
  - **columns:** id, library_id (indexed), mistral_doc_id, filename, mime_type, status (default uploaded, indexed), error, char_count, chunk_count, rules, trace_id, ontology_version, timestamps;
  - **constraints:** unique `(library_id, mistral_doc_id)` as `uq_rag_document`, and the index `ix_rag_documents_library_status`.
- **`ExtractionDraft` (`rag_extraction_drafts`):**
  - **columns:** document_id, payload (JSON `{entities, relations}`), entity_count, relation_count, status (pending|edited|committed), model, rules;
  - **constraints:** unique `document_id`, so there is one draft per document.
- **`LibraryOntology` (`rag_library_ontology`):**
  - **columns:** library_id, version, status (draft|approved|superseded), summary, entity_types (JSON `[{name, description, examples}]`), predicates (JSON `[{name, description, source_types, target_types}]`), prompt, source_document_ids, model, approved_at;
  - **constraints:** unique `(library_id, version)`, and the index `ix_library_ontology_status`.
- **`ExtractionRule` (`rag_extraction_rules`):** library_id (primary key), rules, updated_at.
- **`SystemAgent` (`rag_system_agents`):** key (primary key, e.g. "query_optimizer"), agent_id, name, model, timestamps.
- **`RagEvent` (`rag_events`):**
  - **columns:** trace_id, parent_id, scope (ingest|query), subject (e.g. "document:12"), stage, status (running|ok|failed|skipped), message, meta (JSON), seq, started_at, ended_at, duration_ms;
  - **indexes:** `(trace_id, seq)` and `(subject, started_at)`.

The six models and the status tuples.

## Nuances and gotchas
- **Processing state lives in SQLite** so it survives Neo4j being down.
- **A draft is a mutable proposal,** not a graph.
- **The timeline is append-only and high volume.**
- **Entity identity in Neo4j is `(library_id, normalized, type)`.** That is why the content schema is per library.
- **Predicates were uncontrolled before ontologies.** The same fact came back as "pays" and as "pays_invoice_to", giving two edges.
- **`seq` orders events,** because SQLite timestamps collide.
